event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Teradyne’s 2024 filing still cites the COVID-19 pandemic principally as a potential, forward-looking disruptor rather than an ongoing, quantified drag on performance.  Sentences that reference “health pandemics” or explicitly “the coronavirus” appear in generic risk lists covering international operations and quarterly earnings volatility, and in a broader narrative about threats that could halt shipments or cancel orders.  None of the disclosures provide dollar figures, time-framed downturns, or specific mitigation outcomes; instead they convey that another wave or future pandemic could hurt supply chains, labour availability and customer demand.  Because the pandemic began almost four years before the filing date (placing it at the front edge of the 4-10-year ‘medium-term’ window), the Time Decay Principle caps the evidentiary severity to the mid-range.  Overall, the language signals a material but un-quantified, partially stale risk—substantial enough for continued board-level attention, yet no longer acute or uniquely dominant.  Consequently, individual snippets receive moderate scores (4-6) depending on whether they explicitly link to COVID-19 and describe concrete business impacts.

components.reason: Flags health pandemics as a source of disruption to international sales and operations (aggravating factor).
Appears in the company’s principal risk list, indicating management deems it material.
Generic and un-quantified; no direct COVID-19 mention or data provided (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence acknowledges pandemic disruption but is generic and un-quantified, leading to a mid-level score of 4 within the medium-term window.

evidence_list.snippet: • disruption caused by health pandemics, such as the coronavirus;

components.reason: Explicitly references ‘the coronavirus,’ directly tying the risk to COVID-19.
Frames the threat as a source of operational disruption that can affect quarterly results.
Still generic with no numeric impact or mitigation strategy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct mention of coronavirus plus disruption context merits the upper bound of the medium-term range (6/10).

evidence_list.snippet: Our operations, and the operations of our customers and suppliers, are subject to risks of natural catastrophic events, severe weather, widespread health epidemics, acts of war, terrorist attacks and the threat of domestic and international terrorist attacks, any one of which could result in cancellation of orders, delays in deliveries or other business activities, or loss of customers and could negatively affect our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Identifies ‘widespread health epidemics’ (pandemics) as a risk factor.
Specifies tangible business impacts (order cancellations, delivery delays, loss of customers).
Bundled with many other hazards, diluting pandemic specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete potential impacts but treats pandemics among a broad set of threats; thus a moderate score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: • disruption caused by health pandemics, such as the coronavirus;

components.reason: Directly names coronavirus, showing continued relevance of COVID-19.
Embedded in a list of factors affecting operating results, linking to financial performance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Reiteration of explicit COVID-19 disruption in an operating-results context warrants a score of 6 within medium-term limits.
